Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: In the cross-sectional analysis, serum vitamin C concentration showed no significant association with depression.
Sentence: "In the cross-sectional data, the serum vitamin C concentration was positively associated with the level of attention (r = 0.16, p = 0.02; standardized β = 0.21, p = 0.003), while no significant associations with the levels of fatigue and mood variables being found."
Measured as: depression (mood variables)
Population: Healthy young adults aged 20-39 years (n = 214)
Intervention: Serum vitamin C concentration (measured, not given)
Comparator: Lower vs higher serum vitamin C across participants
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 260
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Winter light therapy reduced depression scores in adolescents.
Sentence: "Winter light therapy increases vitamin D (Δ = 8.2 ng/mL, p < 0.001) and reduces depression (ΔPHQ-9=-3.1, p = 0.005)."
Measured as: depression (PHQ-9)
Population: Chinese adolescents in winter RCTs (N = 200)
Intervention: Winter light therapy
Comparator: Not reported
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 7,321
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported
